title: Dominant sparse-autoencoder features were often harder to explain
summary: In 65.2% of the sparse autoencoders tested, explanations of the highest-contribution quarter of features ranked activation examples less accurately than explanations for the remaining features. The pattern varied by autoencoder architecture.
ai_technology: Sparse autoencoders over pretrained language-model activations

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §3 dominance and explanation tests, §4 Table 2 and Figure 3; same aggregate result in v2

evidence.tested: The study tested a dominance-aware explanation-ranking measure across seven autoencoder architectures and checked robustness to firing-frequency matching and different explanation and judging models.
evidence.unknown: This is an explanation-ranking proxy, not a complete account of each feature’s meaning or its causal role in downstream decisions.
evidence.ai_role: Trained sparse autoencoders represent language-model activations, and model-generated feature explanations are checked using ranked activation evidence.
